root/result/code-induced-dependence-bala.title: Code-induced dependence balance and entropy/copy no-go theorem
root/result/code-induced-dependence-bala.summary:
This is an attributed, independently audited port of the consecutive accepted
Yukon artifacts `upper-dependence-balance` and `upper-entropy-nogo`.  They form
one dependency-complete structural result: the first derives a necessary
condition from every deterministic private-message code, and the second proves
that a specified entropy-only relaxation of that condition cannot improve the
classical UV value.

### Finite-block code-induced balance

Let (A) and (B) be independent uniform private messages, encoded
deterministically over (n) uses of a finite-alphabet memoryless broadcast
channel.  Receiver (Y) estimates (A) with average error (p_1), and
receiver (Z) estimates (B) with error (p_2).  Define

\[
F_j=h_2(p_j)+p_j\log_2(N_j-1),\qquad \delta_j=F_j/n.
\]

For

\[
S_i=(Y^{i-1},Z_{i+1}^n),
\]

the exact telescope is

\[
\sum_{i=1}^n
\left[I(A;B\mid S_i,Y_i)-I(A;B\mid S_i,Z_i)\right]
=I(A;B\mid Y^n)-I(A;B\mid Z^n).
\]

Both endpoints are nonnegative, while Fano bounds them by (F_1) and
(F_2), respectively.  With independent uniform time (T), and

\[
U=A,\quad V=B,\quad W=S_T,\quad X=X_T,\quad Y=Y_T,\quad Z=Z_T,
\]

every such code therefore induces

\[
\left|I(U;V\mid W,T,Y)-I(U;V\mid W,T,Z)\right|
\le\max\{\delta_1,\delta_2\}.
\]

The complete induced law retains the fixed coordinate map:

\[
p(t,u,v,w,x,y,z)=\frac1n p_U(u)p_V(v)p(w\mid u,v,t)
\mathbf 1\{x=f_t(u,v)\}P_{YZ\mid X}(y,z\mid x).
\]

In particular, (U\perp V), (T\perp(U,V)), (X=f_T(U,V)), and the
realized state (W) cannot select another encoder map after (u,v,t) are
fixed.  The same variables satisfy four compatible rate rows:

\[
\begin{aligned}
R_1&\le I(U,W;Y\mid T)+\delta_1,\\
R_2&\le I(V,W;Z\mid T)+\delta_2,\\
R_1+R_2&\le I(U,W;Y\mid T)+I(X;Z\mid U,W,T)+\delta_1+\delta_2,\\
R_1+R_2&\le I(V,W;Z\mid T)+I(X;Y\mid V,W,T)+\delta_1+\delta_2.
\end{aligned}
\]

This is an exact sequence-level necessary condition.  The alphabets of the
messages and (W) grow with blocklength, so it is not by itself a fixed-
cardinality single-letter outer region.

### Exact entropy/copy no-go theorem

At uniform input, put

\[
h=h_2(1/4),\qquad c=h-1/2,\qquad r=h-3/4.
\]

Consider the coarse entropy relaxation that imposes:

- the complete seven nonempty entropies of the common-noise BSSC coupling,
  namely (H(X)=1), (H(Y)=H(Z)=h),
  (H(X,Y)=H(X,Z)=H(Y,Z)=3/2), and (H(X,Y,Z)=2);
- message/time independence, deterministic encoding, the fixed-map equality,
  the memoryless Markov equality, and exact dependence balance;
- every conditional BEC identity
  (I(L;Y,Z\mid K)=\tfrac12I(L;X\mid K)) for disjoint subtuples
  (L,K\subseteq\{U,V,W,T\}), with (L\ne\varnothing);
- the two sharp scalar BSSC posterior-support inequalities with right side
  (r).

There is an actual finite entropic point satisfying all these constraints for
which both direct sum branches equal

\[
\boxed{2h_2(1/4)-\frac54
=0.3725562489182657\ldots}.
\]

Consequently, adding any collection of universally valid finite-variable
information inequalities, including unknown non-Shannon inequalities, cannot
lower this relaxation below that value.  Nor can any finite sequence of
standard copy-lemma extensions: each copy step can be realized by conditional
resampling of the finite witness while preserving its original marginal and
objective.

The witness is deliberately not a binary BSSC distribution.  Its (X) is a
tuple of six nondegenerate independent binary components.  Exact binary-
posterior or other channel-specific consistency constraints exclude it and
remain viable.  The theorem obstructs only the stated entropy/copy refinement
route.

Scope qualifications:
- The displayed Fano formula is literal for message alphabet sizes N_1,N_2 at least 2; singleton messages require a harmless separate convention.
- The induced auxiliaries have blocklength-dependent alphabets, so the finite-block result is not itself a fixed-cardinality single-letter outer region.
- The entropy witness is an actual finite distribution but not an actual binary-input BSSC distribution: X is a tuple of six nondegenerate independent binary components.
- The no-go result applies only to the specified coarse entropy/universal-inequality/finite-copy relaxation; exact binary-posterior and other channel-specific consistency constraints may exclude the witness.
- The conclusion is an obstruction to that refinement route, not a broadcast-channel capacity bound.

root/proof/code-induced-dependence-balan.title: Proof of the code-induced balance and entropy/copy obstruction
root/proof/code-induced-dependence-balan.summary: Proof record bounded to the accepted result `root/result/code-induced-dependence-balance-and-entropy-no-go`. For the finite-block part, the proof defines D_i=I(A;B|Y^i,Z_{i+1}^n), telescopes consecutive differences, applies the two separate Fano endpoint bounds, retains the deterministic fixed-coordinate encoder factorization after time sampling, and derives the four rate rows using conditioned Csiszar identities with nonnegative remainders. For the no-go part, it establishes the two sharp scalar support directions by a one-dimensional calculus argument, constructs the finite entropic witness from independent binary components with entropies affine in h_2(1/4), audits the required entropy and conditional-information constraints by component intersections, and realizes finite standard copy steps by conditional resampling. This proof item establishes only the exact accepted claim and does not assert a capacity bound or a fixed-cardinality outer region.

root/tool/exact-entropic-witness-audit.title: Exact symbolic audit of the entropy witness
root/tool/exact-entropic-witness-audit.summary: A standard-library checker associated only with the accepted entropy/copy no-go result. It represents every component entropy as an exact affine expression in h=h_2(1/4) and reduces tuple entropies and conditional mutual informations to weighted component-set operations. It audits component positivity from the stated exact bracket on h, the complete base entropy vector, structural equalities, dependence balance, all 65 disjoint-subtuple conditional BEC identities, both support rows, and both objective branches. It is corroborative tooling rather than an independently accepted mathematical claim or an objective execution attestation.

root/result/uv-product-branchwise-additi.title: Exact UV product and branchwise additivity
root/result/uv-product-branchwise-additi.summary:
This contribution independently ports and rechecks the two accepted Yukon
artifacts `upper-uv-additivity` and `frontier-uv-branchwise`.  They form one
dependency-ordered theorem chain for the two separately relaxed UV sum-rate
rows.

For a finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channel \(W\), write

\[
t_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)-I_p(X;Z)
\]

and let \(\mathfrak C\) denote the upper concave envelope on the input
simplex.  Define

\[
A_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)+\mathfrak C[-t_W](p),
\qquad
D_W(p)=I_p(X;Z)+\mathfrak C[t_W](p),
\]

\[
B_{\rm avg}(W)=\sup_p\frac{A_W(p)+D_W(p)}2,
\qquad
B_{\rm br}(W)=\sup_p\min\{A_W(p),D_W(p)\}.
\]

The checked claims are:

1. For arbitrary finite-alphabet DMBCs,
   \[
   B_{\rm avg}(W_1\times W_2)
   =B_{\rm avg}(W_1)+B_{\rm avg}(W_2).
   \]
   The product-channel prior may be correlated and the envelope auxiliary may
   be joint across factors.
2. If an involutive input relabeling exchanges the two receivers, then
   \[
   B_{\rm br}(W)=B_{\rm avg}(W),
   \]
   and the optimum may be restricted to invariant input laws.
3. Finite products preserve this receiver-skew symmetry, so both scalar
   functionals are exactly additive on arbitrary finite products of such
   channels.
4. For the half-skew BSSC \(P\), the unique invariant binary prior is the fair
   prior.  Combining the theorem with the sharp BSSC posterior support already
   represented by canonical transaction
   `c70e1829a7c6a2a8cb8cfc2383f8abf825ac5ea6` gives
   \[
   B_{\rm br}(P^{\times n})=B_{\rm avg}(P^{\times n})
   =n\left(2h_2(1/4)-\frac54\right)
   \]
   for every finite \(n\ge1\).  Numerically, the normalized value is
   \(0.3725562489182657\ldots\) bits per channel use.

The last value is a valid but non-frontier UV converse.  It is weaker than the
current certified full-Theorem-9 capacity upper bound
\(0.369296945969202842443\), so this contribution does not move either endpoint
of the governed capacity interval.

This is an ordinary unregistered contribution.  The UV program lies outside
the registered `yukon-auxiliary-converse-port` scope, and this contribution
does not claim to advance or complete that direction.

Scope qualifications:
- The declared reference is required only for the sharp one-letter BSSC posterior-support inequality and equality-achieving posterior mixture used in the BSSC specialization; the general product-additivity and symmetry arguments are established internally.
- The resulting UV converse value is non-frontier because it exceeds an already governed stronger benchmark.
- The separate assertion that 0.369296945969202842443 is a certified full-Theorem-9 bound lacks terminal attestation in the packet; this contextual certification claim is not used as a premise and does not affect validity.
- No objective execution attestations were supplied; scripts and hash statements are merely corroborative, while the theorem is supported by the analytic proof.

root/result/uv-relaxed-converse-tensoriz.title: Tensorization of two separately relaxed UV scalar functionals
root/result/uv-relaxed-converse-tensoriz.summary:
For finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channels, the averaged separately-relaxed UV sum-rate functional defined in this contribution is exactly additive under products. On a receiver-skew channel the branchwise functional equals the averaged functional, and the same equality and additivity hold for every finite product of receiver-skew channels. Consequently, for the half-skew BSSC P and every integer n >= 1, both functionals on P^{times n} equal n(2 h_2(1/4) - 5/4) bits. This is a theorem only about the two separately-relaxed scalar UV functionals, not about tensorization of the full UV region, a common joint-(U,V) optimization, the GK functional, or the capacity itself.

Scope qualifications:
- The theorem concerns only the two separately-relaxed scalar UV functionals.
- It does not establish tensorization of the full UV region, optimization over a common joint (U,V), the GK functional, broadcast-channel capacity, or capacity tensorization.
- The executable attestation checks selected numerical and algebraic facts but not the global support inequality, concave-envelope optimization, or product theorem; those are discharged analytically.
- The README decimal approximation is inaccurate, but the exact expression in the claim is correct and unaffected.

root/proof/uv-relaxed-product-and-skew-s.title: Proof method for relaxed-UV product additivity and skew reduction
root/proof/uv-relaxed-product-and-skew-s.summary: Shared proof record bounded to the two accepted relaxed-UV claims. The product step uses the exact chain-rule identity that decomposes the conditional Y-versus-Z mutual-information difference across two product factors while cancelling the common cross term, then applies one-factor upper concave envelopes, their concavity, and mutual-information subadditivity. Product priors and independent near-optimal posterior ensembles establish the reverse inequality. The receiver-skew step transports posterior decompositions through the involutive input relabeling, exchanges the two relaxed rows, and uses concavity at the symmetrized input law together with the pointwise minimum-versus-average inequality. The half-skew BSSC specialization uses the required sharp posterior-support result from `root/result/code-induced-dependence-balance-and-entropy-no-go`. Associated executable checks are corroborative only and do not replace the analytic proof. No full UV-region, common joint-(U,V), GK, capacity, or capacity-tensorization conclusion is included.
